title: U.S. approves SpaceX plan to deploy 1 million satellites for data centres in space
summary: The Federal Communications Commission (FCC) is authorizing Elon Musk's SpaceX to deploy a constellation of one million satellites for data centres in space, the agency said on Wednesday.

image.caption: The Federal Communication Commission has approved of SpaceX's plan to deploy one million satellites that would serve as data centres in space. Seen here is one of SpaceX's Starlink satellites. (SpaceX)

blocks.text: The Federal Communications Commission (FCC) is authorizing Elon Musk's SpaceX to deploy a constellation of one million satellites for data centres in space, the agency said on Wednesday.
SpaceX already has more than 10,000 Starlink satellites in orbit

Earlier this ‌year, SpaceX sought permission to deploy up to one million orbital compute modules to process massive amounts of data to be used on Earth. The FCC said it was approving the SpaceX “Starmind” constellation to help meet ​rapidly growing demand for AI computing.

Under the licence, SpaceX ​must begin deployment no later than November 2033, deploy 10 per cent of the maximum number — or 100,000 — no later than November 2035 and ​deploy 50 per cent by November 2038, the FCC said.
Approving the application will permit ⁠SpaceX "to pioneer emergent technology ⁠that advances American leadership in space and ‌artificial intelligence," the FCC added.
Data centres are the physical backbone of artificial intelligence, requiring massive amounts of power.

"By directly harnessing near-constant solar power with little operating or maintenance costs, these satellites will achieve transformative cost and ⁠energy efficiency while significantly reducing the environmental impact associated with terrestrial data centres," SpaceX told the FCC.

It was unclear whether SpaceX would put one million satellites in space, where ‌17,000 satellites currently exist. Satellite operators sometimes request approval for higher numbers of satellites than they intend to deploy to buy design flexibility.

blocks.text: SpaceX sought approval for 42,000 Starlink satellites before it began deployment of that system. The growing network currently ​has more than 11,000 satellites in space.
SpaceX's request bets heavily on reduced costs of Starship, the company's ⁠next-generation reusable rocket under development, to help deploy satellites.

Amazon's rival satellite unit Leo and ⁠others have criticized the plan, suggesting SpaceX was unlikely to deploy all the satellites ⁠and ⁠that it could take centuries ​to do so. FCC Chair Brendan Carr rejected that criticism in March.

"Amazon should focus on ​getting Amazon's house in ⁠order with their own launches and their own satellite constellation, rather than worrying about other people that are actually out there launching satellites at the pace and cadence that SpaceX is," Carr said.
The FCC said it was also approving SpaceX's requests to back up its ⁠optical network by approving additional ‌communications.
